title: Endure Trials and Act on God's Word
summary_text: James tells the scattered twelve tribes that trials test faith and build endurance, and that God gives wisdom to those who ask in faith. Wealth fades, but God has promised life to those who endure. Temptation comes from evil desire, which produces sin and death, while God gives good gifts and birth through His true word, making His people a kind of firstfruits of creation. James calls for careful listening and restrained anger, since human anger does not produce God's righteousness. Hearing must lead to action, including controlled speech, care for widows and orphans, and a life unstained by the world.
key_points: Trials develop perseverance, and those lacking wisdom must ask God in faith without divided loyalty.
Riches fade, but those who endure trials are blessed with God's promised crown of life.
Evil desire leads to sin and death; God instead gives good gifts and birth through His word.
James calls for patient listening, restrained anger, and obedience to the word that can save souls.
Pure religion involves controlling speech, caring for distressed widows and orphans, and resisting the world's pollution.

title: Favoritism and Faith Without Deeds
summary_text: Favoring rich visitors over poor ones contradicts faith in Jesus Christ and dishonors people God has chosen to inherit His kingdom. James calls favoritism sin under the law commanding love of one's neighbor, and warns that judgment without mercy awaits the unmerciful. He then challenges a claim to faith that leaves needy believers without food or clothes. Even demons believe in one God, but living faith acts. Abraham's faith worked with his actions and was credited as righteousness; James says Abraham and Rahab were justified by deeds, and concludes that faith lacking deeds is dead.
key_points: James condemns honoring the rich over the poor, noting that rich oppressors also blaspheme the believers' noble name.
Favoritism breaks the law of neighborly love, and those who withhold mercy face judgment without mercy.
A claim to faith that does nothing for a believer needing food and clothing is dead.
James insists on showing faith through deeds; even demons believe that God is one.
Abraham and Rahab were justified by their actions, showing that faith must work with deeds.

title: The Tongue and Wisdom From Above
summary_text: James warns that teachers face stricter judgment and that everyone stumbles in speech. Like a small rudder steering a ship or a spark burning a forest, the tongue has power far beyond its size and spreads wickedness. People use it both to bless God and to curse people made in His likeness, a contradiction James condemns. He contrasts jealous, selfish wisdom, which brings disorder, with wisdom from above, shown through humble deeds, purity, gentleness, and mercy. Those who make peace produce a harvest of righteousness.
key_points: Teachers face stricter judgment, and controlling speech would mean being able to control the whole person.
The small tongue has enormous power to direct life and spread destruction, yet no person can tame it.
Blessing God while cursing people made in His likeness is as contradictory as a spring giving opposite kinds of water.
Jealousy and selfish ambition produce disorder, while heavenly wisdom shows itself in humility, mercy, and peace.

title: Humble Yourselves Before the Lord
summary_text: James traces quarrels, killing, and selfish prayers to desires fighting within people. He calls friendship with the world hostility toward God, who opposes pride but gives grace to the humble. He urges sinners to submit to God, resist the devil, purify their hearts, and mourn their wrongdoing. Slandering a fellow believer places someone above the law, though God alone is Lawgiver and Judge. James then rebukes merchants who boast about tomorrow's profits without acknowledging the Lord's will, and calls knowingly failing to do right sin.
key_points: People covet, fight, and even kill, while their prayers seek resources for selfish pleasures.
Friendship with the world makes people God's enemies, but He gives grace to the humble.
James calls sinners to draw near to God, resist the devil, purify their hearts, and mourn.
Slandering and judging a brother challenges the law and God's place as the only Lawgiver and Judge.
Life is brief and tomorrow uncertain, so business plans depend on the Lord's will rather than human boasting.

title: Judgment, Patient Endurance, and Powerful Prayer
summary_text: James warns rich oppressors of coming misery because they hoard wealth, withhold wages, and have condemned and killed the righteous. He urges believers to wait patiently for the Lord, following the prophets and Job, whose outcome showed the Lord's mercy. He forbids oaths and calls for honest speech, prayer in suffering, and praise in joy. Sick people are to summon the elders for prayer and oil; James says prayer in faith brings restoration and sins are forgiven. Elijah illustrates prayer's power, and bringing a wandering sinner back saves a soul from death.
key_points: The Lord hears unpaid workers, and hoarded wealth testifies against rich people who exploit and murder the righteous.
Believers must wait patiently for the Lord without grumbling, remembering the prophets, Job, and the Lord's mercy.
James forbids swearing oaths and directs suffering people to pray and cheerful people to praise.
Elders should anoint the sick and pray; believers must confess sins and pray for one another's healing.
Turning a sinner back from wandering saves a soul from death and covers many sins.
